title: Denying Self
definition: Denying Self is the disciple's surrender of self-rule, selfish ambition, and sinful independence in order to follow Christ.
summary: Following Jesus requires surrender, not self-enthronement.
christFocus: Jesus Christ calls His disciples to lose their lives for His sake and find true life in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Denying Self describes a Spirit-formed pattern of life for those who belong to Jesus Christ. Christian living is not an attempt to earn salvation but the grateful response of people who have been saved by grace and called to walk with the Lord.

Scripture presents this truth so believers can grow in holiness, endurance, love, wisdom, worship, and mission. It touches the heart, the mind, the tongue, relationships, daily habits, and faithful obedience in ordinary life.

The emphasis of this doctrine is following jesus requires surrender, not self-enthronement.. It points disciples away from self-reliance and toward abiding dependence on Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because discipleship can become shallow when it is reduced to information, emotion, or outward activity alone. Denying Self teaches believers how grace becomes visible in daily conduct, perseverance, relationships, and obedience to Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask the Lord to form this truth in you through Scripture, prayer, repentance, and faithful practice. Let denying self shape how you think, speak, serve, endure, forgive, and represent Christ in the places God has assigned to you.
